The budgetary effects of this Act, for the purpose of complying with the Statutory Pay-As-You-Go Act of 2010, shall be determined by reference to the latest statement titled “Budgetary Effects of PAYGO Legislation” for this Act, submitted for printing in the Congressional Record by the Chairman of the Committee on the 
Budget of the House of Representatives, provided that such statement has been submitted prior to the vote on passage.

fable.w: This is boilerplate PAYGO language that determines budgetary effects by reference to a statement submitted by a House committee chairman. The tempting reading is that a submitted statement and a vote on passage look like procedural input, but every actor is inside Congress and therefore inside the federal government. No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public is consulted, given a hearing, or granted a right to sue.

qwen_block.w: This section describes an internal procedural mechanism for determining budgetary effects using a statement submitted by a Congressional committee chairman. Congress and its committees are part of the federal government, so this interaction is intra-governmental. There is no consultation with or participation by entities outside the federal government.

opus.w: This is standard PAYGO boilerplate that sets how the Act's budgetary effects are measured, using a statement from the House Budget Committee Chairman. The only actors are Congress and its committee, which are inside the federal government. It looks procedural because a statement is submitted before a vote, but no state, expert, company or member of the public takes part in any decision.

opus.b: 1. **Thinking.** The tempting reading is that a statement submitted by the Chairman of the House Budget Committee, before a vote, is a formal step in making a decision. That reading fails because everyone involved is inside the federal government: Congress, its committee, and its chairman. This is standard PAYGO budget boilerplate. No one outside the government is consulted or given a role.

qwen_chat.w: This section establishes a procedural rule for determining budgetary effects by referencing a statement from the Chairman of the House Budget Committee. Since Congress and its committees are part of the federal government, this interaction is internal and does not involve consultation with parties outside the government. It does not grant any right to the public, states, or other external entities to participate in the decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: The budgetary effects of this Act, for the purpose of complying with the Statutory Pay-As-You-Go Act of 2010, shall be determined by reference to the latest statement titled “Budgetary Effects of PAYGO Legislation” for this Act, submitted for printing in the Congressional Record by the Chairman of the Committee on the Budget of the House of Representatives
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that referencing a statement submitted by the Chairman of the House Budget Committee involves an outside party, but the Chairman is a member of Congress, which is inside the federal government. Furthermore, this is a procedural rule for budget scoring, not a mechanism for public or external consultation on a policy decision.
